title: AlphaFold 3 modeling links a monkeypox G9 mutation to weaker complex assembly
summary: AlphaFold 3 modeling of monkeypox virus entry fusion complex proteins predicted that the APOBEC3-type G9 M142I mutation enlarges the interfacial gap and reduces docking stability in the G9/A16/A56/K2 complex. ELISA experiments showed that M142I significantly reduces G9 binding to A16 and impairs recruitment of A56/K2. The authors state that direct functional assays are still needed to determine the effect on viral entry.
ai_technology: AlphaFold 3 monomer, binary and quaternary complex structure modeling
organization: BSL-3 Laboratory (Guangdong), School of Public Health, Southern Medical University, Guangzhou, China

evidence.tested: ELISA binding experiments testing the structure-predicted weakening of G9 interactions.
evidence.unknown: Net effect of the mutation on viral entry and fitness; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: AlphaFold 3 predicted the mutant complex structures that guided the binding experiments.
